title: Grill — CSV export for invoices
summary:
Before this gets planned: **11 decisions** the build would otherwise make silently, plus one that only matters if you export internal notes. Start with the **Blocking** one and the two that **shape the plan**; the confirm list at the end is defaults I'd bet on — one click each.

Source: ticket `BILL-412` (committed as `docs/specs/invoice-csv-export.md`).

proven.text: **No background job needed.** The export query runs in 4.2 s over 50k invoices on a copy of prod-sized seed data, under the 10 s request timeout.

proven: Invoices are already tenant-scoped through `scopedQuery()` (`src/billing/invoices.ts:22`), so the export inherits isolation by reusing it.

sections.title: Scope & business rules
sections.intro: These decide which rows the file contains, so they shape the query and the tests.

questions.title: Should invoices of soft-deleted customers appear in the export?
questions.why: Decides the WHERE clause and whether the billing-period totals in the file match the dashboard.
questions.context: The dashboard total **includes** them (`reports/usage.sql:40` has no `deleted_at` filter), but the customer list hides them. If the export drops them, its totals won't match the dashboard for any month with a churned customer.

evidence.label: dashboard query: no deleted_at filter
evidence.code:
SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount_cents)
FROM invoices
JOIN customers USING (customer_id)
WHERE period = $1
GROUP BY customer_id;

options.label: Include them, flagged
options.description: Rows stay, with a `customer_status` column reading `deleted`.
options.consequence: Totals match the dashboard; one extra column.

options.label: Leave them out
options.description: Same rows the customer list shows.
options.consequence: Totals stop matching the dashboard for churned months.

options.label: Let the user choose
options.description: A checkbox on the export dialog, off by default.
options.consequence: One more UI state to build and test.

recommendation.reason: Finance reconciles the file against the dashboard, and a flag column keeps that true without hiding anything.

questions.title: Which time zone decides whether an invoice falls inside the selected date range?
questions.why: An invoice issued at 23:30 on the 31st lands in a different month depending on the answer.

options.label: The tenant's configured time zone
options.description: `tenants.timezone`, already used by the monthly statement.

options.label: UTC
options.description: What the database stores; simplest query.

recommendation.reason: The monthly statement already uses it (`src/billing/statement.ts:61`), so both documents agree on what 'March' means.

questions.title: Which optional columns go in the file?
questions.why: Each one is a join and a test; the required columns (number, date, customer, amount, currency) are always in.

options.label: Internal notes
options.description: Free text, may hold staff comments.

recommendation.reason: These are what the two finance tickets that asked for this (BILL-398, BILL-405) mention.

questions.title: Who may export the internal notes column?
questions.why: Notes can hold staff-only comments; exporting them widens who can read them.
questions.context: Today only the `billing_admin` role can see notes in the UI (`src/billing/policy.ts:12`). The export endpoint would be reachable by every role that can open the invoices page.

options.label: billing_admin only
options.description: Same rule as the UI; the column is absent for everyone else.

recommendation.reason: Keeps today's access rule; widening it is a separate decision.

questions.title: What's the most rows one export may contain before we refuse and ask the user to narrow the range?
questions.why: Above ~200k rows the response passes the 10 s timeout, and the plan would need a background job after all.

recommendation.reason: Twice the largest tenant's yearly volume (48k), and well inside the measured timeout.

questions.title: What does the user see when the range exceeds that limit?
questions.placeholder: The exact message, or what it should convey

recommendation.value: This range has more than 100,000 invoices. Pick a shorter date range and export again.
recommendation.reason: States the limit and the fix; matches the tone of the existing import errors.

questions.title: If we have to cut one thing to ship this sprint, rank what matters most.

options.label: Opens cleanly in Excel (UTF-8 BOM, `;` locales)

recommendation.reason: A wrong total is a support ticket; a slow download is an annoyance.

questions.title: Do you have a CSV finance already imports into their accounting tool? Drop it here.
questions.why: Matching their column order and date format saves a round of rework.

questions.title: Anything that has to be true before you'd call this done, beyond the acceptance list in the spec?
questions.placeholder: e.g. finance signs off on a sample file

sections.title: Confirm or override
sections.intro: Low-stakes defaults I'd bet on. Confirm with one click, or override with what it should be.

recommendation.value: UTF-8 with BOM, comma-separated, amounts as decimals with a dot
recommendation.reason: The BOM makes Excel read accents correctly; the importer in `src/import/csv.ts` already parses this shape.

recommendation.value: Each export writes an `invoice.exported` audit event with the range and row count
recommendation.reason: Every other bulk read in billing does (`src/audit/events.ts:30`).
